plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), that together depict the complete bonding framework in acetylene (C2H2), distinguishing the sigma bonds formed by sp hybrid orbitals from the two pi bonds formed by unhybridized p orbitals. Panel (a) shows the individual orbital interactions: three σ bonds are labeled — two C–H σ bonds at the outer ends of the molecule and one C–C σ bond in the center, all formed by the end-on overlap of sp hybrid orbital lobes (orange) meeting at the two carbon atom centers (black dots) — while four unhybridized p orbitals (rendered as red and blue lobes extending above, below, and to the sides of the C–C axis) overlap side by side in two perpendicular planes, with dashed lines connecting opposite lobes to indicate the lateral overlap regions that constitute the two π bonds. Panel (b) shows the overall spatial appearance of the bonding: the orange σ-bond lobes form a linear framework through the molecule, while one π bond (red lobes) wraps above and below the C–C axis and a second π bond (blue lobes) extends in front of and behind the axis, each labeled "One π bond" and "Second π bond" respectively, together encircling the C–C σ bond. This figure establishes the C≡C triple bond in acetylene as the combination of one σ bond and two mutually perpendicular π bonds, and demonstrates how sp hybridization leaves two unhybridized p orbitals per carbon available for the side-on overlaps that enforce the linear molecular geometry.

interactions.label: Bonding view
interactions.teaches: The C≡C triple bond is built by first aligning the sigma framework along the molecular axis, then adding two mutually perpendicular pi overlaps around it
A sigma bond comes from end-to-end overlap and contributes one bond order unit, while each pi bond comes from side-to-side overlap and adds one more unit to the C-C triple bond
The two pi bonds occupy perpendicular planes around the same C-C axis rather than lying in a single flat overlap

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a horizontal H-C-C-H axis. Approximate world coordinates: left H at x=-3.0, left C at x=-1.0, right C at x=1.0, right H at x=3.0. Carbon centers are small black spheres radius ~0.06. Hydrogen atoms are pale blue spheres radius ~0.28. Sigma sp lobes are orange/yellow #f6b23a to #ffd36b, elongated teardrop ellipsoids aligned along x; each major lobe length ~0.9 and width ~0.38. C-H sigma overlaps sit between x=-3.0 to -1.0 and x=1.0 to 3.0; C-C sigma overlap is centered at x=0. In panel a, show the sigma framework plus individual p orbitals at each carbon: red p_y lobes extend vertically above and below each carbon, with lobe centers around y=±0.75 and z=0; blue p_z lobes extend in the perpendicular front/back direction, rendered diagonally in the axonometric view with centers around z=±0.65 and slight screen-down offset. Red color #ee6a72, blue color #6f9fd8, both semi-gloss with soft transparency. Add dark gray minus signs on visible p lobes. Dashed overlap guides are gray #666666, running horizontally between left and right p lobes at the corresponding upper/lower/front/back positions. In panel b, replace the separated p orbitals with smooth continuous pi clouds: red bond as two rounded capsule-like lobes above and below the C-C axis spanning x≈-1.35 to x≈1.35, y≈±0.65, z≈0; blue bond as two similar capsule-like lobes in front/behind the axis spanning x≈-1.35 to x≈1.35, z≈±0.55. Keep the orange sigma framework visible through/inside the pi clouds. Labels should match the source placement: sigma labels above the three orange overlaps in panel a; 'One π bond' above-left with leader lines to the red cloud in panel b; 'Second π bond' above-right with leader lines to the blue cloud. Dominant palette: white background, black text/leader lines, orange sigma lobes, red pi lobes, blue pi lobes, pale blue hydrogens.
interactionPlan.notes: Use an orthographic axonometric camera with the molecule axis locked horizontally at the default view; allow orbit interaction but include a reset-to-source-view affordance if available. Orbital lobes can be built from scaled metaballs, ellipsoids, or custom lathed teardrop meshes with soft transparent materials. For panel switching, do not display both textbook panels at once; keep the same molecule centered and swap/merge the orbital representations. Click targets should include: left C-H σ, central C-C σ, right C-H σ, red π bond, and blue π bond. On click, tint or outline the selected region and show a callout such as 'C-C σ bond: end-to-end sp-sp overlap, contributes 1 to C-C bond order' or 'π bond: side-to-side p-p overlap, contributes 1; two π bonds plus one σ give bond order 3.'

authoredContext:
In molecules with sp hybrid orbitals, two unhybridized p orbitals remain on the atom ( ). We find this situation in acetylene, H−C≡C−H , which is a linear molecule. The sp hybrid orbitals of the two carbon atoms overlap end to end to form a σ bond between the carbon atoms ( ). The remaining sp orbitals form σ bonds with hydrogen atoms. The two unhybridized p orbitals per carbon are positioned such that they overlap side by side and, hence, form two π bonds. The two carbon atoms of acetylene are thus bound together by one σ bond and two π bonds, giving a triple bond.

(a) In the acetylene molecule, C 2 H 2, there are two C–H σ bonds and a C ≡ C triple bond involving one C–C σ bond and two C–C π bonds. The dashed lines, each connecting two lobes, indicate the side-by-side overlap of the four unhybridized p orbitals. (b) This shows the overall outline of the bonds in C 2 H 2 . The two lobes of each of the π bonds are positioned across from each other around the line of the C–C σ bond.

Two diagrams are shown and labeled, “a” and “b.” Diagram a shows two carbon atoms with two purple balloon-like orbitals arranged in a plane around each of them, and four red balloon-like orbitals arranged along the y and z axes perpendicular to the plane of the molecule. There is an overlap of two of the purple orbitals in between the two carbon atoms. The other two purple orbitals that face the outside of the molecule are shown interacting with spherical blue orbitals from two hydrogen atoms. Diagram b depicts a similar image to diagram a, but the red, vertical orbitals are interacting above and below and to the front and back of the plane of the molecule to form two areas labeled, “One pi bond,” and, “Second pi bond,” each respectively.

Hybridization involves only σ bonds, lone pairs of electrons, and single unpaired electrons (radicals). Structures that account for these features describe the correct hybridization of the atoms. However, many structures also include resonance forms. Remember that resonance forms occur when various arrangements of π bonds are possible. Since the arrangement of π bonds involves only the unhybridized orbitals, resonance does not influence the assignment of hybridization.

discrepancies: The central C–C σ overlap in panel (a) is much smaller and more diamond-like than the broad orange overlap shown in the source.
The blue and red p orbitals in panel (a) are too tightly superimposed in the rendered view, making the perpendicular p-orbital sets less clearly separated than in the source.
Panel (b) represents the π bonds as smooth capsule/tube-like clouds rather than the flatter, lobed electron-density shapes with tapered ends and stronger occlusion cues in the source.
The generated view relies on toggling between (a) and (b), so the original side-by-side comparative composition is not visible by default.
evaluation.notes: The figure is conceptually correct and interactive, but several orbital proportions and the side-by-side textbook composition are not fully faithful.
action_items: Enlarge and smooth the central C–C σ overlap so it resembles the broad orange bonding region in the source.
Adjust the red and blue p orbitals in panel (a) so the perpendicular sets are more visually separated and match the source offsets.
Replace the panel (b) capsule π clouds with flatter, tapered lobed surfaces that better match the red and blue electron clouds in the source.
Consider adding a side-by-side comparison mode showing panels (a) and (b) together.
